topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, outlines the scope of the lecture on cancer causes, and presents the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer as an Evolutionary Genetic Disease and Endogenous Mutational Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a microevolutionary genetic process and explore how endogenous metabolic stress, cell replication, and inherited genetic predispositions generate oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Epidemiology, and the Cancer Risk Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of environmental carcinogens in cancer development, analyzing geographic incidence patterns, migrant data, and the debate over mutational bad luck versus preventable exposure.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents induce malignancy, highlighting the specific mechanisms of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria co-infection in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical, Dietary, and Physical Mutagens and Xenobiotic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical agents damage DNA directly or require host xenobiotic metabolism to generate reactive adducts and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Multistage Carcinogenesis, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumor promotion, two-stage carcinogenesis, developmental timing vulnerabilities, and summarize the overall pathways of cancer causation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating Carcinogenicity and Mutational Signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the experimental, computational, and population-based tools used to identify and prove carcinogenicity, including whole-genome mutational signatures, biobanks, animal models, and the Ames test.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reflecting on personal and societal risk-benefit assessments regarding carcinogenic exposures and summarizing the final takeaways.
